feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-10 design (score 700.19, best raced so far), unchanged in every field. Its evidence is from iteration 10: oval 20/20 (mean 1.97 s, max_error 0.0096), s-bend 20/20 (mean 2.32 s, max_error 0.0205), and slalom 0/20 (progress 0.53, 1.35 line-loss events per run, off track in every run). Iterations 7 (kp 5.0, kd 1.0) and 8 (16 mm sensors at +/-4 cm) each lost s-bend finishes and scored lower, so both are past their useful range. Iterations 9 and 10 showed that moving the sensors forward (y 0.06 to 0.07 to 0.075) gave small gains with no completion loss. Because no iteration follows this one, a regression could not be corrected, and the candidate is the only validated design that keeps 20/20 completions on both development tracks. The slalom gap is the main lost score, but it cannot be closed with an untested change at this point. Decision: approve, so the race runs the validated design. If the race shows the expected 20/20 on oval and s-bend, no further change is needed. Measurements to read from the race are the slalom loss location (max_error and line_loss_events) and steering_oscillation on s-bend, which together would have guided the next iteration had one existed.
requested_changes: No change requested. Race the iteration-10 design unchanged, since it is the best validated design (score 700.19) and no later iteration exists to correct a regression.

Contingency for the record only: if s-bend completions were to fall below 20/20 in the race, the iteration-9 sensor position (y 0.07) with the same controller is the next-best validated fallback, since iteration 10 differs only by the y step.
